description.summary: vibrant content blended with what is behind it

protocol.description:
Lets a client have a surface's content blended with what the compositor has already drawn behind it, instead of painted over it: the vibrancy of labels and glyphs on a material, which take on the colour of the frosted backdrop under them.
It is meant for a subsurface holding only greyscale content (labels, glyphs, fills) above a surface whose background is a translucent material. Coloured content blends unpredictably.
With plus_darker the surface holds the amount to darken by, not the colour to darken with: a grey c at alpha a that should darken as Apple's plus-darker does (D + c - 1) is drawn as white, 1 - c, at alpha a, so the compositor takes a(1 - c) away from what is behind.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects made with it are unaffected.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the surface already has a vibrancy object

request.name: get_vibrancy

description.summary: make a vibrancy object for a surface

request.description: A surface has at most one vibrancy object; asking for a second one while the first is alive is the already_constructed error.

interface.name: niri_vibrancy_v1

description.summary: how a surface blends with what is behind it

interface.description: The mode is double-buffered state, applied on the surface's next commit. A new object's mode is none. Destroying it sets the mode back to none on the next commit. Once its surface is destroyed the object is inert.

entry.name: plus_lighter
entry.summary: added to what is behind, clamped: light content brightens it

entry.name: plus_darker
entry.summary: subtracted from what is behind, clamped at 0: the content is how far each pixel darkens

request.name: set_mode
request.description: An unknown mode is treated as none.
